Food Chemistry and Biochemistry; Carbohydrate Chemistry; Functional Food Ingredients; Biorefinery and Cereal By-products
Valorisation of Cereal Bran Hemicellulose Streams for Functional Food and Feed Applications

A cross-border project investigating the conversion of wheat and rye bran hemicelluloses into prebiotic oligosaccharide ingredients and dietary fibre concentrates for food and animal feed use. Bulatović led the work package on enzymatic and chemical hydrolysis processes and product characterisation. Hungarian partners contributed microbial screening and feed trial design. The project established protocols for comparing GH10 and GH11 xylanases on substrates of differing botanical origin and produced data on energy use and process economics at 50 L pilot scale.
Alkali extraction of arabinoxylan from wheat bran: effect of NaOH concentration and extraction time on yield and molecular weight distribution

Wheat bran arabinoxylan (AX) was extracted using aqueous NaOH at concentrations ranging from 0.5 to 4 M and extraction times of 1–6 hours at 30 °C. Yield of water-extractable AX increased from 8.4 % to 21.7 % (w/w dry bran) as NaOH concentration rose to 2 M, but levelled off above this point. Size-exclusion chromatography coupled with refractive index detection showed a bimodal molecular weight distribution at lower alkali concentrations, collapsing to a single population (Mw 280–320 kDa) at 2 M NaOH. The arabinose-to-xylose (A/X) ratio, determined by gas chromatography after acid methanolysis, remained within 0.55–0.62 across all conditions, suggesting limited side-chain cleavage. Phenolic acid content (ferulic and p-coumaric acids, measured by reversed-phase HPLC) decreased markedly above 1.5 M NaOH, indicating saponification of ester linkages. Optimal conditions for retaining molecular integrity while achieving acceptable yield were identified as 1.5 M NaOH, 3 hours, yielding 18.2 % AX with Mw 410 kDa. The extracted fraction was characterised as a suitable substrate for subsequent hydrolysis studies.
